summary: Remote-controlled shell over WebRTC via hardcoded third-party signaling relay
details: When `vanexa-agent start` runs, the daemon opens a WebSocket to a hardcoded signaling relay at https://vanexa-agent-relay.tubefood.workers.dev, negotiates a WebRTC DataChannel to a paired remote peer, and executes commands received over that channel through child_process spawn/exec on the installer's host. The signaling relay is a Cloudflare Workers subdomain under an account named `tubefood`, not the package publisher `@vanexalabs-ai` — the operator of that relay is an implicit trust anchor in the pairing handshake and can observe ICE/SDP metadata (including client IPs) for every daemon that starts. The result is a network-to-shell channel giving a paired remote party terminal execution, filesystem, git, and desktop-automation control on the installer's machine with the user's privileges. README advertises the phone-driven command-execution capability, but the third-party-controlled relay hostname and lack of an installer-configurable default place the trust boundary outside the publisher.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
